# Shared library — `lib_survey_fg_density_functions.R`

Sourced by `01_biomass.R`, `02_fisheries.R`, `03_pbqb-traits.R` and `04_diets.R`; has **no top-level driver code** of its
own — every symbol below is a function definition only.

## FG-matching functions

Every observed species runs through this cascade, in order, until it
resolves to a Functional Group or falls through to manual review — the
diagram shows the actual fallback order implemented in the code below
(same style as `medbs_pipeline_methodology.qmd`'s `@sec-fg-matching`
diagram; each stage only attempts species the previous one left
unmatched).

```{=html}
<div class="mermaid">
%%{init: {'flowchart': {'padding': 20, 'nodeSpacing': 60, 'rankSpacing': 90}, 'themeVariables': {'fontSize': '18px'}}}%%
flowchart LR
    A1["match_species_to_fg()&lt;br/&gt;direct ScientificName match"] --> A2["match_nominate_subspecies_fg()&lt;br/&gt;strip repeated trinomial word, retry"]
    A2 --> A3["apply_seed_fg_rules()&lt;br/&gt;manual rules, zero-reference FGs"]
    A3 --> A4["fallback_match_fg_by_taxonomy()&lt;br/&gt;Genus to Phylum, exactly-one-FG rule"]
    A4 --> A5["summarize_unresolved_species()&lt;br/&gt;manual review"]

    classDef purple fill:#EEEDFE,stroke:#534AB7,color:#26215C
    classDef gray fill:#F1EFE8,stroke:#5F5E5A,color:#2C2C2A
    class A1,A2,A3,A4 purple
    class A5 gray
</div>
```

| Function | Purpose | Returns |
|---|---|---|
| `validate_survey_data(dataframe1, dataframe2, strata = TRUE)` | Fail-fast schema/uniqueness check on the two standardized input tables (required columns present, `SampleID` unique per survey) | `invisible(TRUE)` |
| `prepare_fg_lookup(dataframe2)` | Deduplicates species→FG reference; keeps genuine stanza splits (a species exclusively mapped to ≥2 FGs), excludes/flags ambiguous multi-FG species | deduped `data.table(ScientificName, FG_num, FG_name)` |
| `match_species_to_fg(dataframe1, fg_lookup_safe)` | Direct left-merge by `ScientificName` | merged `dt` |
| `match_nominate_subspecies_fg(dt, fg_lookup_safe)` | Strips a repeated trinomial word (e.g. "Diplodus sargus sargus" → "Diplodus sargus") and retries the match | `dt` with newly resolved rows |
| `fetch_taxonomy(species_names, taxonomy_source = "worms")` | Dispatches to `fetch_taxonomy_worms()`, `fetch_taxonomy_fishbase()`, or both | `data.table(ScientificName, Genus, Family, Order, Class, Phylum)` |
| `fallback_match_fg_by_taxonomy(dt, fg_lookup_safe, taxonomy_source = "worms", rank_levels = c("Genus","Family","Order","Class","Phylum"))` | Data-driven rank fallback — a rank value is used only if it maps to exactly one FG among reference species | `dt`, with `attr(dt,"fetched_taxonomy")` and `attr(dt,"still_unresolved_taxonomy")` attached |
| `apply_seed_fg_rules(dt, dataframe2, seed_rules, species_exceptions = NULL)` | Explicit small rule table for FGs with **zero** reference species (nothing for the automatic fallback to learn from); species-level exceptions applied first | `dt` |
| `summarize_unresolved_species(dt, taxonomy = NULL)` | Mean biomass + appearance count per still-unmatched species, sorted by appearance count | summary `data.table` |
| `build_fg_manual_review_template(csv_out_dir, out_path = file.path(csv_out_dir, "FG_manual_review_template.xlsx"))` | Combines `survey_unmatched_for_manual_review.csv` + `medias_unmatched_for_manual_review.csv` into one de-duplicated review workbook, with blank `GF`/`FG_name` columns ready to hand-fill | invisibly returns the combined `data.table`; writes an `.xlsx` |

`build_fg_manual_review_template()` is a one-off, run-it-yourself helper, not
part of the automated pipeline — nothing calls it from `01_biomass.R` itself.
After a run leaves species unmatched, call it against that run's
`output/biomass/` folder to get one workbook (a `README` sheet plus a
`For_review` sheet, sorted by how often each species actually showed up in
the data — review the highest-impact species first). Its `ESPECIE`/`GF`/
`FG_name` columns deliberately use the exact same names as `FG_WMed_2026.csv`'s
own sheet 4 (`fg_wmed_95`) — fill in `GF`/`FG_name` for whichever species you
want to resolve, then copy columns A:C straight into a **new** version of
that sheet (never overwrite the original in place), and point `fg_file` at
the new file for the next run. There's no code path that writes the filled-in
review back into `FG_WMed_2026.csv` automatically — that hand-off is deliberately
manual, since it's a genuine judgment call about which FG a given species
belongs to.

| `snapshot_full_extent_species(matched_dt, species_taxonomy, source_label, csv_out_dir, sci_name_col = "ScientificName")` | One row per distinct species a source's own FG-matching step saw, taken BEFORE that source's `FILTER_AREAS`/year restriction — i.e. every species anywhere in the raw file(s) that source loaded, independent of this run's config. Called once each for MEDITS (Steps 3-4), MEDIAS (Step 9), and stock assessment | writes `all_species_<source>_full_extent.csv` |
| `build_full_fg_species_catalog(csv_out_dir, out_path = file.path(csv_out_dir, "FG_WMed_full_species_catalog.csv"))` | Combines the three `all_species_*_full_extent.csv` snapshots above into ONE species catalog — matched species (a real `FG_number`/`FG_name`) and still-unmatched species (`FG_number`/`FG_name` blank) together, with a `sources` column (e.g. `"MEDITS+MEDIAS"`) showing which source(s) actually observed each one. Note the column is named `FG_number` here (not `GF`, as in `FG_WMed.xlsx`/`build_fg_manual_review_template()` above) since this catalog spans all three sources rather than being a direct fill-in template for the Excel sheet | invisibly returns the combined `data.table`; writes a CSV |

`01_biomass.R` calls `build_full_fg_species_catalog(csv_out_dir)` itself,
near the very end (Step 14, right after `trim_workbook_to_final_sheets()`)
— **`FG_WMed_full_species_catalog.csv`** lands in `output/biomass/` on every
run without any extra step. It's a candidate "sheet 4" replacement covering
every species — matched (`status = "matched"`, already correctly resolved)
and unmatched (`status = "needs review"`, blank) — in one file, sorted with
matched rows first. Same read-only relationship to `FG_WMed_2026.csv` as
`build_fg_manual_review_template()` above — nothing writes back into it
automatically.

Unlike the matched/unmatched CSVs everything else in this script reads and
writes, the three `all_species_*_full_extent.csv` snapshots — and so this
catalog — are **NOT scoped by `FILTER_AREAS`/`YEAR_ECOPATH`/`TS_YEARS`**, by
construction: `snapshot_full_extent_species()` is called right after each
source's own FG-matching step and *before* that source's own area
restriction (MEDITS: before `dt <- dt[AreaID %in% FILTER_AREAS]`; MEDIAS:
`acoustic_matched` itself is never restricted in place, only derived summary
tables are; stock assessment: `star_wm` is already the whole West Med
subregion, not this run's `FILTER_AREAS`). So this catalog always covers the
**whole available survey extent** — every GSA and year the raw MEDITS/
MEDIAS/stock-assessment files actually contain — on every run, regardless
of what region/years that particular run happens to be configured for. A
source's snapshot (and its contribution to the catalog) simply won't exist
for a run where that source didn't execute at all — `AREA_MODE == "custom"`
skips MEDIAS and stock assessment entirely, so a custom run's catalog is
MEDITS-only there, which is a real limit of that mode (no MEDIAS/stock-
assessment data exists to catalog), not something a wider `FILTER_AREAS`
would fix.

## Area / stratum / density functions

| Function | Purpose | Returns |
|---|---|---|
| `match_samples_to_area(dt, area_shp, area_id_col)` | Spatial join (`sf::st_join`) of sample points to polygons; no-op if `AreaID` already fully populated | `dt` |
| `assign_depth_stratum(dt, strata_def)` | Bins `Depth` into strata via `findInterval()`; out-of-range depths → `Stratum = NA` | `dt` |
| `filter_samples_by_area(dt, area_filter, filter_type = c("shapefile","bbox"), points_crs = 4326)` | Custom sub-region filter, independent of GSA/`AreaID` | `dt` filtered to in-area `SampleID`s |
| `compute_sample_densities(dt)` | `Density := Biomass / Effort` | `dt` |
| `apply_catchability_correction(dt, catchability_table, default_q = 1, species_taxonomy = NULL, exempt_fg_names = NULL, exempt_species = NULL)` | 5-tier resolution: direct species → genus "spp" entries → explicit broad-rank entries → taxonomic-proximity fallback → `default_q`; exemptions override last. Divides `Density`/`Biomass` by resolved `q` | `dt` |
| `remove_sample_outliers(dt, threshold = 70, min_samples = 5, drop_outliers = TRUE, log_scale = TRUE)` | Per-species/per-area robust z-score (median/MAD) on `log1p(Density)`; sets flagged `Density`/`Biomass` to `NA` if `drop_outliers = TRUE` | `dt`, with `attr(dt,"flagged_outliers")` |
| `compute_fg_densities_by_stratum(dt, strata = TRUE)` | Sums species density within FG per sample, then across samples by area/year/[stratum]/FG | `per_group_fg` (`density_sum`) |
| `compute_strata_area_by_area(area_ids, area_shp, area_id_col, strata_def, cache_path = NULL, resolution = 1)` | Downloads NOAA bathymetry per area, bins cell area into depth strata (latitude-corrected); optional CSV cache | `strata_area_by_area` table |
| `weight_by_strata(per_group_fg, n_samples_by_stratum, strata_area_by_area)` | Core strata-weighted estimator: `D_area = Σ_h (density_sum_h/n_samples_h) · area_prop_h` | `fg_index`, with `attr(fg_index,"per_stratum")` |
| `simple_area_density(per_group_fg, n_samples_by_area)` | Unstratified path (`strata = FALSE`) | `data.table` |
| `weight_by_area(fg_index_stratified)` | Region-wide weighting from absolute stratum areas (`per_stratum` attribute); denominator = area of all cells sampled that year (`sampled_area_by_year` attribute), so zero catches count (fixed 2026-10-07) — requires the stratified path upstream | `fg_index_regional` |
| `sampled_area_by_year(n_samples_by_stratum, strata_area_by_area)` | Area of the (area, stratum) cells with ≥ 1 haul per year — denominator of the region-wide means | `data.table(Year, sampled_area_km2)` |
| `flag_ts_upward_spikes(year, x, half = 2, k = 3, min_fold = 3)` | One-sided Hampel filter on log values; used by `export_ecopath_ecosim_excel(spike_filter = TRUE)` to blank isolated spikes in Ecosim B series | logical vector |
| `compute_species_densities_by_stratum(dt, strata = TRUE)` / `weight_species_by_area(per_group_sp, n_samples_by_stratum, strata_area_by_area)` | Species-level analogs of the two functions above, feeding the `FG_spp` sheets | `data.table(Year, FG_num, FG_name, ScientificName, mean_density)` |
| `compute_cv_log_by_fg(value_dt, value_col, min_replicates = 2)` | `cv_log = sd(log1p(x))/mean(log1p(x))` per FG/Year, averaged across years — feeds the Ecosim "Weight" row | `data.table(FG_num, FG_name, cv_log, n_years)` |

## Plotting functions

| Function | Produces |
|---|---|
| `plot_sample_map(dt, area_shp, area_id_col, ..., by_year = FALSE, selected_areas = NULL, land_on_top = FALSE)` | Sample coverage map, points colored inside/outside the study area, polygons shaded by sample intensity |
| `plot_fg_timeseries_by_area(fg_index, ...)` / `plot_fg_timeseries_regional(fg_index_regional, ...)` | Faceted FG density time series, per-area vs. region-wide |
| `plot_strata_profile(fg_index_stratified, strata_def, ...)` | Depth-strata validation bar chart (pre-area-weighting, per-sample density by stratum) |

## Excel workbook functions

`ecopath_ecosim_inputs.xlsx`
carries **only the 10 final target sheets** — every native/intermediate
table each block used to also keep as a workbook sheet is now CSV-only
(see "Per-block output CSV subfolders" and "Final target sheet order"
below). The table below reflects the current function signatures, not the
older ones this document used to describe.

| Function | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `upsert_workbook_sheets(sheets, out_path)` | Adds/replaces the named sheets in `out_path`, **leaves every other sheet untouched**. Creates the workbook if it doesn't exist yet. Safe to call repeatedly, from any script, in any order. |
| `write_native_sheet_csv(dt, name, out_dir)` / `write_native_sheets_csv(sheets, out_dir)` / `read_native_sheet_csv(name, out_dir)` | Generic CSV read/write for a block's own native/intermediate tables — `out_dir` is always passed explicitly by the caller (the block's own subfolder), never assumed |
| `read_existing_ts_years(out_path, sheet_name, csv_dir = NULL)` | Reads year values from column 1 of an existing native CSV sheet (e.g. `Ecosim`), so `Catches_Ecosim`'s years stay aligned with it. `csv_dir` defaults to `dirname(out_path)` for back-compat; the numbered scripts pass the correct block's subfolder explicitly |
| `read_full_fg_reference(out_path, csv_dir = NULL)` | Reads `FG_lookup.csv` (a biomass-block output) — the full FG_num/FG_name reference, used to expand PB_QB/FG_References/etc. to every model FG, not just the ones with data this run |
| `export_ecopath_ecosim_excel(fg_index_regional, species_density_regional, n_samples_by_area_year, dataframe2, year_ecopath, ts_years, out_path, species_taxonomy = NULL, fg_cv_log = NULL, normalize_ts = TRUE, csv_out_dir = NULL)` | Writes the final `Ecopath_B` sheet directly to the workbook, plus native/intermediate CSVs (`FG_spp_Ecopath`, `FG_lookup`, `Ecosim`, `FG_spp_Ecosim`, a `PB_QB_spp` scaffold) into `csv_out_dir` (01_biomass.R's own `output/biomass/` subfolder) |
| `add_catches_to_ecopath_workbook(fg_catch, fg_lookup, out_path, year_ecopath, area_km2, ts_years = NULL, fleet_structure = NULL, csv_out_dir = NULL, biomass_csv_dir = NULL)` | Converts raw catch tonnes to t/km² density; writes native CSVs `Catches_Ecopath`/`Catches_Ecosim`/`Fleet_Structure` into `csv_out_dir` (02_fisheries.R's `output/fisheries/`). Reads `Ecosim.csv` from `biomass_csv_dir` when `ts_years` isn't passed explicitly |
| `add_pbqb_to_ecopath_workbook(fg_weighted, out_path, species_pb_qb = NULL, csv_out_dir = NULL, biomass_csv_dir = NULL)` | Writes native CSVs `PB_QB`/`PB_QB_spp` into `csv_out_dir` (03_pbqb-traits.R's `output/pbqb-traits/`). Reads `FG_lookup.csv` from `biomass_csv_dir` to expand to every model FG |
| `finalize_ecopath_ecosim_summary_sheets(out_path, year_ecopath, biomass_csv_dir = NULL, fisheries_csv_dir = NULL)` | Builds the final `Ecosim_ts` sheet by combining native CSVs from **two** blocks — `Ecosim` (biomass) plus `Catches_Discards_FG_ts`/`Catches_Ecosim`/`Fishing_Effort_by_Fleet` (fisheries) — hence the two separate directory arguments. Guards against a blank/non-numeric Year cell in `Ecosim.csv` (which would otherwise crash the relative-scaling-reference comparison) by falling back to raw, un-rescaled kW-days for that fleet with an explicit message. |
| `build_fg_references_sheet(out_path, biomass_csv_dir = NULL, fisheries_csv_dir = NULL, pbqb_csv_dir = NULL, diet_csv_dir = NULL)` | Builds the final `FG_References` sheet — one row per FG, consolidating which data source fed each block (see "The FG_References sheet" below) |
| `trim_workbook_to_final_sheets(out_path)` | **Run last**, by every numbered script. Reduces the workbook to exactly the 10 final target sheets (see below), dropping any native/intermediate sheet a much older run of this workbook might still be carrying |

## Per-block output CSV subfolders

Every native/intermediate CSV a block writes now lands in that block's own
subfolder under the shared `out_dir`, instead of a single flat directory
shared by all scripts:

* `01_biomass.R` (+ `01b`) → `output/biomass/` (plots `output/plots/biomass/`)
* `02_fisheries.R` → `output/fisheries/` (plots `output/plots/fisheries/`)
* `03_pbqb-traits.R` → `output/pbqb-traits/`
* `04_diets.R` → `output/diet/` (plots `output/plots/diets/`)
* `05_validation.R` → `output/validation/` (plots `output/plots/validation/`, including the P/B–Q/B, F and P/Q plots built from 03's CSVs)
* a custom-region run (`AREA_MODE = "custom"`) writes to `output/<AREA_NAME>/`

`ecopath_ecosim_inputs.xlsx` itself stays at the top-level `output/` — all
four scripts read and write it, so it has no single owning block. Each
script defines its own `csv_out_dir` near the top and passes it (or a
`*_csv_dir` pointing at a *different* block's subfolder, for the handful of
cross-block reads — species density, strata area, `FG_lookup.csv`,
`Ecosim.csv`, `biomass_proportion_by_species_fg.csv`, catch time series)
into the library functions above. Every one of those new directory
arguments defaults to `dirname(out_path)` (the workbook's own top-level
folder) when omitted, so nothing breaks if some other caller doesn't pass
them.

## Final target sheet order (11 sheets)

`target_order`, used by `trim_workbook_to_final_sheets()` / `finalize_workbook_sheet_order()` at the end of every numbered script (order confirmed by the 2026-10-07 logs):

1. `info` — run metadata (areas, countries, YEAR_ECOPATH, TS_YEARS, …)
2. `FG_spp` — FG × species × taxonomy and biomass share, written by `01_biomass.R`
3. `Ecopath_B` — FG biomass (t/km²), 1994–1996 mean, with a `Reference` column
4. `Ecopath_L` — FG × fleet landings, `02_fisheries.R`
5. `Ecopath_Di` — FG × fleet discards, `02_fisheries.R`
6. `Ecopath_PBQB` — FG P/B, Q/B and their sources, `03_pbqb-traits.R`
7. `Ecopath_traits` — species traits under FG header rows, `03_pbqb-traits.R`
8. `Ecopath_diet` — predator FG × prey FG, `04_diets.R`
9. `Ecosim_ts` — B, catch and effort series
10. `FG_References` — per-FG sources (`B_ref`, `L_ref`, `Di_ref`, `PBQB_ref`, `PBQB_method_ref`, `traits_ref`, `diet_ref`), built last by `04_diets.R`
11. `Ecobase` — EcoBase values used for comparison (reference only)

Every native/intermediate table (`Ecopath`, `Catches_Ecopath`, `PB_QB`,
`Ecosim`, `Catches_Ecosim`, `Fishing_Effort_by_Fleet`, `FG_spp_Ecopath`,
`FG_spp_Ecosim`, `FG_lookup`, `traits_ewe`, `fg_traits_weighted`,
`PB_QB_spp`, `References` [species-parameter-level, `03_pbqb-traits.R`'s
own audit CSV — a different table from the `FG_References` workbook sheet
above, despite the similar name], `Ecobase`, `Catches_Discards_FG_ts`,
`diet_references_by_fg`, ...) lives only as CSV, in its own block's
subfolder, never as a workbook sheet — `trim_workbook_to_final_sheets()`
drops anything else it finds regardless.

## The FG_References sheet

Built by `build_fg_references_sheet()`
(`lib_survey_fg_density_functions.R`), run by `04_diets.R` after every other
script has had a chance to run. One row per FG, with columns:

| Column | What it summarizes | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `FG_num`, `FG_name` | The full FG reference | `FG_lookup.csv` (`output/biomass/`) |
| `B_ref` | Which biomass source (MEDITS/MEDIAS survey vs. stock assessment) fed `Ecopath_B`/`Ecosim_ts`'s B block for this FG | `biomass_source` in `survey_fg_annual_index_regional_combined.csv` (`output/biomass/`) |
| `L_ref`, `Di_ref` | Which catch/discard source (GFCM/FDI/SAU-derived vs. stock assessment) fed `Ecopath_L`/`Ecopath_Di`/`Ecosim_ts`'s catch time series for this FG | `catch_source` in `Catches_Discards_FG_ts.csv` (`output/fisheries/`) |
| `PBQB_ref`, `traits_ref` | Whether `PB_FG`/`QB_FG` came from the empirical species-level calculation or an EcoBase literature gap-fill | `PB_source`/`QB_source` in `PB_QB.csv` (`output/pbqb-traits/`), falling back to a generic "empirical" note when EcoBase gap-filling didn't run |
| `diet_ref` | Which diet studies (metaweb references, MAISHA study citations, FishBase/SeaLifeBase references) fed this FG's column in `Ecopath_diet` | `diet_references_by_fg.csv` (`output/diet/`), rolled up from `build_species_diet()`'s per-predator citations via the same species→FG mapping the diet matrix itself uses |
| `PBQB_method_ref` | The calculation METHOD/literature behind `PB_FG`/`QB_FG` (as opposed to `PBQB_ref`, which is about the *data*, not the method) | `dispatch_group` in `PB_QB_spp.csv` (`output/pbqb-traits/`), mapped to a literature citation |

Each column is a best-effort summary (distinct values `" | "`-joined when a
FG drew on more than one source across years/species/studies), not a full
audit trail — the individual block's own CSV named in the table above has
the complete detail. A column is left blank for a FG when the block behind
it hasn't run yet against this workbook, with a message saying so rather
than an error; running `build_fg_references_sheet()` again later (as
`04_diets.R` does every run) fills in whatever is available by then.

# Script 5 — `04_diets.R`

**Role:** Step 4. Builds the predator FG × prey FG diet matrix and the `FG_References` sheet. Auto-runs on `source()`. Sources `lib_survey_fg_density_functions.R`, `lib_worms_taxonomy_lookup.R`, `lib_fishbase_diet_matrix.R` and `03b_ecobase.R`. Must run after `01_biomass.R` (species biomass shares and `Ecopath_B`).

## Configuration

| Variable | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `METAWEB_XLSX_PATH` | `data/Complementary data/data_entry_metaweb_empty.xlsx` | metaweb (empty template) |
| `DIET_FALLBACK_ENABLE_MAISHA` | `TRUE` | use MAISHA |
| `MAISHA_PATH` | first existing of `data/diet/MAISHA/MAISHA_DwC-A`, `…/MAISHA_DwC-A.zip`, any `maisha*.xlsx/csv` under `data/diet` (case-insensitive) | MAISHA location |
| `DIET_FALLBACK_ENABLE_FISHBASE` | `TRUE` | use FishBase/SeaLifeBase |
| `DIET_FISHBASE_METHOD` | `"fg_matrix"` | build the FG matrix with `lib_fishbase_diet_matrix.R` |
| `DIET_FALLBACK_ENABLE_ECOBASE` | `TRUE` | try EcoBase diet matrices |
| `DIET_TAXON_SPLIT` / `DIET_CATEGORY_SPLIT` | `"equal"` / `"biomass"` | split of a prey taxon / food category over its FGs |
| `DIET_DETRITUS_MAX_TL` | 3 | detritus dropped for predators with TL ≥ 3 |
| `DIET_METRIC_PRIORITY` | `diet_metric_priority.csv` | IRI > %W > %N > %FO > presence |

## Inputs

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `<pcloud_dir>/data/FG_WMed_2026.csv` | species → FG and taxonomy |
| `<pcloud_dir>/data/Complementary data/data_entry_metaweb_empty.xlsx` | metaweb (`DATA_ENTRY`, `Taxonomic_codes`, `Non_taxonomic_groups`) |
| `<pcloud_dir>/data/diet/MAISHA/MAISHA_DwC-A` | MAISHA v1.2 Darwin Core Archive: `occurrence.txt` (one "Predator" record per study × predator, `occurrenceRemarks == "Predator"`, with citation, date and coordinates, listing its prey records in `associatedOccurrences`; prey records carry the WoRMS `scientificName`) and `extendedmeasurementorfact.txt` (per prey: gravimetric %, numerosity %, frequency of occurrence; per predator: the unknown/debris/detritus fractions — detritus kept as a prey item, unknown and debris dropped) |
| FishBase/SeaLifeBase (`rfishbase`) | DIET, DIETITEMS, FOODITEMS; cached as `output/diet/fishbase_diet_raw_*.csv` |
| `<pcloud_dir>/data/Complementary data/diet_reference_tables/fishbase_food_category_to_fg.csv` | food-category regex → FG rules (about 44), including non-food exclusions |
| `output/biomass/biomass_proportion_by_species_fg.csv`, workbook `Ecopath_B` | $b_{s|f}$ and $B_j$ |
| `<pcloud_dir>/data/ewe_group_table.csv` (optional) | predator flag override |

## Method

See [DIET — Ecopath_diet sheet / diet matrix] above and `medbs_pipeline_methodology.qmd` (Diet Matrix) for the equations. In short: tier per predator FG (metaweb → MAISHA → FishBase/SeaLifeBase → EcoBase); study proportions by the first available metric; prey → FG by species, then taxonomic rank (equal split), then food category (biomass split), then a WoRMS second pass (`worms_diet_prey_cache.rds`); eggs and larvae → zooplankton; detritus dropped for TL ≥ 3; studies averaged; species weighted by biomass share; columns renormalised to 1.

## Outputs (in `output/diet/`)

| File | Content |
|---|---|
| `MAISHA/`, `FishBase/` | each source alone: species-level diets, FG matrix (long/wide), item mapping and unassigned items (REVIEW) |
| `external_diet_matrix_fg_long.csv`, `external_diet_matrix_fg_wide.csv` | MAISHA + FishBase combined (used in `Ecopath_diet`) |
| `external_diet_item_mapping_REVIEW.csv`, `external_diet_unassigned_items_REVIEW.csv` | how each prey item was assigned / not assigned |
| `diet_provenance_by_predator_fg.csv`, `diet_references_by_fg.csv` | tier and studies per FG |
| `diet_still_missing_REVIEW.csv`, `diet_cannibalism_REVIEW.csv`, `diet_matrix_column_sum_REVIEW.csv` (only written when a column ≠ 1) | checks |
| `diet_composition_ewe.csv` | EwE import format |
| workbook `Ecopath_diet`, `FG_References` | final sheets |
| `plots/diets/diet_matrix_heatmap.png` | heatmap |

## Key functions

| Function | File | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `maisha_diet_records()` | `lib_fishbase_diet_matrix.R` | reads MAISHA (DwC-A folder/zip, or a flat table), tags Mediterranean studies by coordinates (lon −6 to 36.5, lat 30 to 46; non-Mediterranean studies are dropped when the predator has Mediterranean ones), returns study × predator × prey rows with W/N/FO |
| `fb_fetch_diet_tables()`, `fishbase_diet_records()` | `lib_fishbase_diet_matrix.R` | FishBase/SeaLifeBase tables with per-server DietCode joins; Mediterranean studies first |
| `diet_resolve_prey()` | `lib_fishbase_diet_matrix.R` | prey item → FG weights $w_{k \to j}$ |
| `diet_records_to_fg_matrix()` | `lib_fishbase_diet_matrix.R` | species diets → FG matrix, with the WoRMS second pass |
| `write_diet_source_outputs()` | `lib_fishbase_diet_matrix.R` | writes each source's files |
| `build_species_diet()`, `build_fg_diet()` | `04_diets.R` | metaweb tier |
| `export_ewe_matrix_csv()`, `build_ecopath_diet_sheet()` | `04_diets.R` | exports |
| `build_fg_references_sheet()` | `lib_survey_fg_density_functions.R` | `FG_References` |

# Script 6 — `05_validation.R`

**Role:** Step 5. Reads the workbook and the REVIEW files of 01–04; changes no input sheet.

- **STEP A** — compares `Ecopath_B`, `Ecopath_PBQB` (and L/Di when the reference has them) with the "estimates" sheet of the 1995 Western Mediterranean model (`WMed_EwE.xlsx`, $A_{old}$ = 846,002 km²). Old → new groups via `validation_reference_tables/old_to_new_fg_crosswalk.csv` (many → one summed, one → many compared with the sum). Old densities are also expressed on the new area, $X_{old}\,A_{old}/A_{new}$ (same total tonnes). Flags ratios outside 0.5–2. Plots: `biomass_vs_old_model_by_fg.png` (both values side by side, same total tonnes) and `…_as_published.png`.
- **STEP B** — `validation_summary_ALL.csv`: index of every check (P/B, Q/B, GE; P/Q; diet sums; cannibalism; missing diets; EcoBase evaluations; FGs without B; even species splits; temporal mismatches; fleet coverage; zero-catch FGs; unmatched names).
- **Block 11** — total zooplankton field check against Fernández de Puelles et al. 2023 (*Water* 15:4267): field 2–17 mg DM/m³ over the mean sampled depth $z_{eff}$ = 86.7 m, DW:WW 0.1–0.2 (ASSUMPTION), compared with FGs 68 + 69 + 71 + 72; salp upper bound with salp DW:WW 0.0804. Output `zooplankton_total_field_check_REVIEW.csv`.
- **STEP C** — one PNG per check and `plots/validation/validation_plots_ALL.pdf` (19 pages), also embedding the P/B–Q/B, F, P/Q and diet plots.

Outputs in `output/validation/`: `comparison_with_old_westmed_estimates_REVIEW.csv`, `biomass_vs_old_model_REVIEW.csv`, `old_workbook_unmatched_fg_names_REVIEW.csv`, `validation_summary_ALL.csv`, `zooplankton_total_field_check_REVIEW.csv`.

# Status of the 2026-10-07 run and open issues

All five scripts completed without errors (logs `20261007_094022_01_biomass_log.txt` to `20261007_100250_05_validation_log.txt`). Changes made after this run — **rerun 02 → 03 → 05**:

1. `02_fisheries.R` — F and the NEI F ≤ 1 cap use the final `Ecopath_B` (adult hake FG 27 now gets an F; macrozooplankton and suprabenthos are no longer capped against survey bycatch). Residual fleet column renamed "Target countries - fleet not resolved". "6 target countries" wording removed from messages.
2. `03_pbqb-traits.R` — FG-level F from `F_by_fg.csv` added to P/B of non-fish FGs with catch (cephalopods, shrimps, lobsters, molluscs, macrobenthos); invertebrate Q/B recomputed as 3 × P/B. Previously this step only ran with a retired catch file, so these FGs had P/B without fishing mortality.
3. `05_validation.R`, `01b_biomass_unsurveyed.R` — comments and the residual column name brought up to date.
4. `lib_survey_fg_density_functions.R`, `01_biomass.R` (evening of 2026-10-07) — **rerun 01 → 05**. Region-wide MEDITS and MEDIAS densities now count zero catches: the denominator is the area of all cells sampled that year, not only the cells where the FG was caught. This lowers `Ecopath_B` of patchy or depth-restricted FGs: in an offline test the 1994–1996 means were ×1.7 too high at the median and ×3 or more for 17 FGs. F, P/B and the balance change with them. New Ecosim trend rules (haul cap at q95, years with < 80 % area coverage blank, upward-spike filter) change only the B series, not `Ecopath_B`; see `ecosim_haul_cap_effect_REVIEW.csv`, `survey_area_coverage_by_year.csv` and `ecosim_ts_spikes_removed_REVIEW.csv`.

Open issues, by block:

| Block | Issue | Where to look |
|---|---|---|
| F | Deep-water rose shrimp F = 5.86 (catch 3,713 t/yr, B 0.0036 t/km²) | `F_by_fg.csv`; MEDITS q; NEI decapod split |

# Methodology document — `medbs_pipeline_methodology.qmd`

A Quarto write-up of the method (R chunks `eval: false`, except the setup chunk that copies figures and outputs). It documents `lib_survey_fg_density_functions.R` and `01_biomass.R` in both `AREA_MODE`s (FG matching, study area, haul density, catchability, outliers, stratified and regional estimators, MEDIAS), then one section per script with its equations and references (Biomass with `01b`, Fisheries, PB/QB, Diet, Validation) and the status and open issues of the latest run. It embeds the GFCM GSA GeoJSON (from `export_gsa_boundaries.R`) in a Leaflet map with a client-side configuration generator. The setup chunk copies figures from `out_dir/plots/<block>/` (and `out_dir/<AREA_NAME>/plots/` for the custom example) into `figures/`, and key outputs into `downloads/`, so the rendered HTML is portable.

# Appendix: Adapting this pipeline & other library files

*(Moved here from the main body — useful for a future maintainer retargeting this pipeline to a different region, not needed to follow the demo.)*

## Other library files

### `lib_worms_taxonomy_lookup.R`

Library file, no top-level driver code — `source()`'d automatically by the
numbered scripts. Defines a single function:

**`worms_taxonomy_lookup(names_vector)`** — the single taxonomy source used
everywhere in the pipeline (so genus/family comparisons are always
apples-to-apples, never a FishBase-derived family compared against a
WoRMS-derived one for the same actual family). Strips `"Genus spp."`
suffixes so genus-level placeholders still resolve, chunks the query list
(50 names/chunk) against `worrms::wm_records_names()`, picks the best
(`status == "accepted"` preferred) match per name, and returns
`data.table(original_name, search_term, AphiaID, matched_name, rank, status,
phylum, class, order, family, genus)`. Explicitly namespaces `purrr::map()`
rather than calling `map()` bare — the `maps` package (loaded elsewhere in
this pipeline for basemap plotting) also exports an unrelated `map()`, and
whichever package attached most recently silently wins an unqualified call.

### `lib_build_species_df_from_survey.R` (retired — not in the repository)

No longer used: `03_pbqb-traits.R` builds `species_df` itself (see Script 4, step 2). Former description, kept for reference: library file — bridges `01_biomass.R`'s survey output and
`03_pbqb-traits.R`'s PB/QB estimation. Defines:

**`build_species_df_from_survey(survey_csv_path, year_ecopath_range,
out_rds_path = NULL)`** — reads `species_density_regional_combined.csv`,
restricts to `YEAR_ECOPATH`'s snapshot years (the same years used for the
`Ecopath` sheet's Biomass column, so PB/QB weighting and the reported Biomass
describe the same time snapshot), collapses to one mean-density `Biomass`
value per species (stops with an error if any species maps to more than one
FG within that year range — shouldn't happen given upstream FG-matching
logic), sets `Yield := NA` (this survey pipeline has no catch/landings data
of its own — F = Yield/Biomass isn't computable from it directly). Optionally
saves the result as an `.rds`. Returns
`species_df(Species, FG, FG_name, Biomass, Yield)`.

---

## Standalone cartography utilities (not part of the numbered pipeline)

### `export_gsa_boundaries.R`

Standalone — does not need `01_biomass.R` or the shared
library sourced first. Downloads the same GFCM GSA shapefile via the same URL
and GSA-numbering fix (`SMU_CODE` 111/112 → 11). **Western-Med-specific as
delivered:** restricts to GSA 1–11 — change the `gsa_num %in% 1:11` filter to
any other GSA range to export a different region's boundaries. Simplifies
the result for web embedding via
`rmapshaper::ms_simplify(keep = 0.05, keep_shapes = TRUE)` (keeps small
polygons like Alboran Island, GSA 2, from being deleted outright), and writes
`gsa_boundaries.geojson` — the file embedded in
`medbs_pipeline_methodology.qmd`'s interactive Leaflet map.

### `fig_WMed_basemap.R` (not in the repository)

Standalone map-generation script (not sourced by anything else), purely
cartographic — not required by the numbered pipeline at all.
**Western-Med-specific as delivered:** downloads the GFCM GSA shapefile,
splits polygons into Western Med (GSA 1–11, the target study area) vs.
context GSAs (12, 16 — Northern Tunisia, South of Sicily) and draws the
Sicily Channel divide (Cape Bon–Cape Lilibeo) as the Western/Central
Mediterranean boundary; all three of those choices would need editing to
produce an equivalent basemap for a different region. The general
technique — label placement via the "pole of inaccessibility" algorithm
(`polylabelr`, more robust than `st_point_on_surface()` for narrow,
coastline-hugging GSAs) plus a high-resolution (`rnaturalearthhires`)
coastline — is reusable as-is for any region. Output:
`output/plots/westmed_gsa_map.png`.

## Adapting this pipeline to a different region

Everything below applies whether the target region is a single GSA, an
arbitrary GSA subset, the whole Mediterranean GSA-by-GSA, or a fully
custom (non-GSA) boundary.

### Preferred method: source the scripts with pre-set options

`01_biomass.R`, `02_fisheries.R`,
`03_pbqb-traits.R`, `04_diets.R` and `05_validation.R` are **source-able**: every region/year/method knob each
one uses (`FILTER_AREAS`, `TARGET_COUNTRIES`, `YEAR_ECOPATH`,
`START_YEAR`/`END_YEAR`, `TS_YEARS`, `DATASET_VERSION`,
`TARGET_COUNTRIES_OVERRIDE`, `OUTLIER_METHOD`, `PB_QB_SELECTION_MODE`, `MACROZOO_SOURCE`, `MAISHA_PATH`,
`out_dir`/`pcloud_dir`/`git_dir`, and a handful more — each script's own
"Configuration" section, under a comment block headed `SOURCE-ABLE
SCRIPT`, lists exactly which variables it recognizes) is wrapped in
`if (!exists("VAR", envir = .GlobalEnv, inherits = FALSE)) VAR <- <default>`.
That means:

* If a variable is **already set** in the calling environment before the
  script is `source()`-d, the script uses that value and skips its own
  default entirely.
* If it is **not set**, the script falls back to its original Western Med
  default (GSA 1–11, 1994–2023) — running any of the three scripts on its
  own, exactly as before, is completely unchanged.

`run_pipeline_demo.R` is a driver script demonstrating this: it sets
`out_dir`/`pcloud_dir`/`git_dir` once, then `source()`s
`01_biomass.R` → `02_fisheries.R` →
`03_pbqb-traits.R` → `04_diets.R` in that dependency order (01 must run
first — see [Adapting this pipeline to a different region] below and each
script's own header comment for why; 04 specifically needs 01's
`FG_spp_Ecopath` sheet in the shared workbook for its species'
share-of-FG-biomass values, and is otherwise optional — diet composition
isn't needed for every run). It includes two ready-to-run examples,
switched via a `RUN_MODE` flag at the top:

* `RUN_MODE <- "westmed_default"` — sets nothing beyond the three paths;
  every script uses its built-in West Med default.
* `RUN_MODE <- "custom_example"` — sets `FILTER_AREAS <- 17:18`,
  `TARGET_COUNTRIES <- c("Italy", "Croatia", "Slovenia")`,
  `YEAR_ECOPATH <- 2005:2007`, `TS_YEARS <- 2000:2020`, and
  `START_YEAR`/`END_YEAR <- 2000`/`2020` as a worked Adriatic-GSA example
  — copy and adapt this block for any other region/year range, setting
  only the variables that need to differ from the West Med default.

`YEAR_ECOPATH` in particular is read by all three scripts and must stay
consistent across them (it defines the single Biomass snapshot the PB/QB
weights are computed against) — setting it once in the driver script
before any of the three are sourced keeps them in sync automatically,
which is easy to forget when editing each script's hardcoded copy by hand.

This sourcing approach and the manual per-script editing approach
described in the rest of this section are not mutually exclusive — the
`if (!exists(...))` guards mean a variable can still be hardcoded by
editing the script directly (equivalent to always setting it), or left
alone to pick up a caller's override, on a variable-by-variable basis.

**To model a different GSA or set of GSAs** (Adriatic, Ionian, Aegean,
Levant, or the whole basin), starting from `01_biomass.R` as
a template:

* `FILTER_AREAS` — set to the target GSA number(s). No other GSA-based code
  in `lib_survey_fg_density_functions.R` hardcodes a Western-Med-only
  assumption — `compute_strata_area_by_area()`, `weight_by_strata()`,
  `weight_by_area()` etc. are all region-agnostic and operate on whatever
  `area_ids`/`area_shp` they're given.
* `ALBORAN_GSAS`/`fix_alboran_longitude_sign()` — a Western-Med-only
  correction (GSA 1–3); harmless no-op elsewhere, delete if not needed.
* `MEDIAS_HANDBOOK_AREAS`/`GSA_AREA_CROSSWALK` — only populated for Western
  Med GSAs; add the target region's own rows from the MEDIAS Handbook
  (or rely entirely on the bathymetry-derived 10–200 m fallback if MEDIAS
  data or handbook-reported areas aren't available for that region).
* `out_dir`/`pcloud_dir`/`git_dir` paths, and the raw MEDITS/MEDIAS/FG-
  reference file paths under them — point at the target region's own data.
* `export_gsa_boundaries.R` — optional cartography
  only; edit the GSA-range filters if you want an equivalent map for the
  new region, otherwise skip it (nothing downstream needs it).

**To model a fully custom (non-GSA) region anywhere in the Mediterranean**,
set `AREA_MODE <- "custom"` before sourcing `01_biomass.R`, plus `AREA_NAME`,
`CUSTOM_AREA_TYPE` (`"bbox"` (default), `"shapefile"`, or `"gsa"`), and
`CUSTOM_BBOX`/`CUSTOM_SHAPEFILE_PATH`/`CUSTOM_GSA_IDS` set to the target
boundary — see [`AREA_MODE == "custom"`] above. No GSA-specific code path
is involved for `"bbox"`/`"shapefile"` (the Alboran-sign fix is present but
is a documented no-op outside GSA 1–3); MEDIAS and stock-assessment biomass
are skipped entirely under `AREA_MODE == "custom"`, regardless of
`CUSTOM_AREA_TYPE`.

Everything downstream of Step 1 — `02_fisheries.R`, `03b_ecobase.R`,
`03_pbqb-traits.R`, and the shared library's Excel-export/PB-QB functions — is
already region-agnostic: they operate on whatever `strata_area_by_area.csv`
and `species_density_regional_combined.csv` Step 1 produced, with no
Western-Med-specific logic beyond `02_fisheries.R`'s GFCM division codes
(37.1.1–37.1.3) and `GSA_COASTAL_STATE` table (which country is the coastal
state of which GSA; `TARGET_COUNTRIES` is derived from it and from
`FILTER_AREAS`) — both need checking for another region — and `03b_ecobase.R`'s
`MED_LON_MIN/MAX`/`MED_LAT_MIN/MAX` bounding box (already covers the **full**
Mediterranean by default — Gibraltar to the Levant — so it does not need
editing for a sub-region; narrow it only if you specifically want to exclude
literature models from elsewhere in the basin).
